title: Goat Curry
subtitle: Caribbean slow-cooked goat curry with scotch bonnet and warming spices
excerpt: The flagship curry of the Caribbean: goat shoulder braised low and slow with scotch bonnet, curry powder, allspice, and thyme until the meat is tender and falling from the bone in a deep, spiced sauce. Standard Sunday cooking across the Caribbean diaspora.

recipe.sourceNotes: Goat curry occupies a central position in Caribbean cooking, particularly in Jamaica, Trinidad, Guyana, and across the Caribbean diaspora in Britain. The curry tradition of the Caribbean arrived with Indian indenture workers brought to the Caribbean after the abolition of slavery in the nineteenth century, particularly to Trinidad and Guyana, where Indo-Caribbean communities developed their own curry traditions with local ingredients. In Jamaica, curry goat developed slightly differently, incorporating the jerk spice tradition (allspice, scotch bonnet) alongside Indian curry spices. Goat is ideal for long slow cooking: it has more fat marbling than British lamb and stands up to prolonged braising without becoming mushy. The meat should be sourced on the bone if possible; bone-in goat adds enormous body to the sauce.

recipeTools.notes: A large, heavy casserole with a lid.

content.text: Cook low and slow: goat on the bone needs at least 2 hours, and 2.5 hours gives a better result. The meat should be tender enough to fall from the bone but not disintegrating. Brown the meat in batches rather than crowding the pan; moisture will steam rather than colour if the pan is too full. The scotch bonnet can be left whole (mild-ish heat) or chopped (fiery).

items.preparation: bone-in, cut into 5 cm pieces by the butcher
left whole for moderate heat, chopped for fiery

content.text: Mix the goat pieces with 2 tablespoons of the curry powder, the allspice, salt, and pepper. Leave to marinate for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.

Heat the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Brown the goat in batches until deeply coloured. Remove and set aside. Reduce the heat to medium, add the onion, and cook for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, and remaining 1 tablespoon of curry powder and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomato purée and cook for 1 minute.

Return the goat to the casserole. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, scotch bonnet, spring onions, and thyme. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 2 to 2.5 hours until the goat is very tender and starting to fall from the bone. Remove the scotch bonnet (if left whole) and thyme. Serve with rice and peas.
